chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was brought a pickpocket who had stolen dirhams from a man's sleeve. He said: 'If he had stolen it from his outer shirt, I would not cut his hand, but if he had stolen it from his inner shirt, I would cut his hand.'

key_terms.أَقْطَعَهُ: He cut it (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for amputating the hand in Islamic theft law regarding the garment worn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential principle of 'khufya' (concealment) in the hadd punishment for theft, where Imam Ali (AS) differentiates between superficial removal from the outer garment and deep concealment from the inner layer. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the thief's intent and the degree of secrecy as criteria for imposing the full corporal penalty, reflecting a nuanced application of Quranic law.
